first_principles_point: Real estate is not space. It is a legal claim on a scarce place that someone needs to use and can keep paying for.
money_path: tenant/customer/location need -> lease, rent, access, or usage payment -> property owner/REIT/operator -> operating cost, capex, debt service -> AFFO/cash
company_examples: American Tower; Prologis; Equinix; Welltower; Realty Income; VICI; Simon Property; Digital Realty
proof_needed: occupancy; rent collection; leasing spreads; escalators; AFFO; tenant credit; debt maturity; cap rates; development yield; churn
safe_use: Use as a no-background real estate chapter frame, not as proof that every scarce location earns durable cash.

first_principles_point: Space is abundant in theory; usable place is scarce when activity needs that location, permit, route, power node, customer flow, or demographic catchment.
money_path: needed activity -> specific usable place -> rent/access payment -> maintenance and financing -> cash
company_examples: towers; logistics warehouses; data centers; senior housing; net lease; venues
proof_needed: occupancy; utilization; tenant need; replacement supply; lease duration; capex
safe_use: Safe claim: location value is use-case plus cash durability.

first_principles_point: Physical presence turns location and calendar capacity into scarce inventory: seats, rooms, venues, tables, gates, convention space, and destination access.
money_path: event/travel/social need -> scarce place/time slot -> ticket, room, venue, or rent payment -> operator/landlord -> cash after labor/debt/capex
company_examples: VICI; Host Hotels; Disney Experiences as reference; Live Nation as reference; MGM as services link
proof_needed: attendance; occupancy; RevPAR; advance bookings; deferred revenue; rent coverage; capex; debt
safe_use: Safe claim: presence can create location premium, but only if usage and cash conversion support it.

company_examples: Equinix; Digital Realty; NextEra/FPL; AEP; Williams as old-site reference; utilities; midstream
proof_needed: power capacity; interconnection; bookings; colocation revenue; tariff/recovery; capex; customer concentration
safe_use: Safe claim: grid access and power availability can become location scarcity.

first_principles_point: Healthcare real estate is valuable when aging demand, patient access, operator staffing, reimbursement, and local affordability support the property cash stream.
money_path: senior/patient need -> care location or senior housing -> resident payment, operator rent, or reimbursement-supported rent -> landlord/operator -> AFFO/cash
company_examples: Welltower; Ventas; Healthpeak; medical office; senior housing operators
proof_needed: occupancy; same-store NOI; operator margin; labor cost; payer/reimbursement; rent coverage; resident affordability
safe_use: Safe claim: aging can support location demand, but operator economics must be proven.

first_principles_point: Real estate is a preferred private-capital destination because it can be financed, levered, leased, appraised, securitized, and sold as a cash-yielding asset.
money_path: pension/insurance/private fund capital -> property vehicle or REIT -> asset acquisition/development/debt -> rent/fee/sale/refinancing -> platform and investor cash
company_examples: Blackstone; Brookfield; KKR; Apollo; Realty Income; private RE funds
proof_needed: AUM; deployment; debt; cap rates; NOI; realizations; fee income; tenant cash; collateral
safe_use: Safe claim: private capital routes money into property claims, but asset-level returns require schedules and cash proof.

first_principles_point: The tenant is the cash engine. A location is only as valuable as the activity inside it and the payer behind it.
money_path: tenant activity -> revenue/cash -> rent payment -> landlord debt/capex/dividend -> AFFO
company_examples: Realty Income; Simon Property; Prologis; Welltower; American Tower
proof_needed: tenant credit; rent coverage; occupancy; collections; same-store NOI; churn; bankruptcies
safe_use: Safe claim: real estate analysis must start with tenant payment ability.

first_principles_point: A lease is a legal wrapper that turns use of place into a scheduled claim on future cash.
money_path: use right -> lease contract -> base rent/escalator/reimbursement -> landlord cash -> debt service/AFFO
company_examples: Realty Income; American Tower; Prologis; Welltower; VICI
proof_needed: lease duration; escalators; renewal spreads; tenant concentration; collection; straight-line rent; AFFO adjustments
safe_use: Safe claim: lease terms matter as much as the property type.

first_principles_point: Real estate often fails through financing before it fails through physical use. Higher rates can break the spread between property yield and funding cost.
money_path: property income -> interest expense/refinancing -> residual cash -> dividend or reinvestment
company_examples: all REITs; net lease; data centers; hotels; senior housing
proof_needed: debt maturity; fixed/floating mix; interest rate; secured debt; liquidity; AFFO payout; capex
safe_use: Safe claim: debt maturity is a central real estate proof field.

first_principles_point: Scarcity only matters if replacement is hard. New supply, zoning, permits, power, labor, and capital decide whether rent power lasts.
money_path: demand -> existing asset rent -> possible new supply -> rent pressure or durability -> cash
company_examples: Prologis; Equinix; American Tower; hotels; senior housing; data centers
proof_needed: supply pipeline; permits; development yield; construction cost; power availability; market rent; absorption
safe_use: Safe claim: scarce location requires a replacement-supply test.
